definition: In the context of property law, a profit, or profit à prendre, is a nonpossessory interest that allows a person to enter another’s land and remove natural resources or products such as minerals, timber, sand, crops, or fish. A profit differs from a possessory interest, which conveys immediate rights of occupancy or control. A profit is related to an easement but grants the additional right to take something of value from the land. It may be created by express grant, reservation, or prescription and may exist as appurtenant, meaning it runs with the land, or in gross, meaning it is personal and independent of land ownership.  property  French term wex professional corporation / profit (property rights) Dictionary compilation | 26 September 2026
